historical_references.reference: The Hindu goddess Mridani is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. In one chapter, she is described as the goddess of the Earth, and is invoked by the hero Bhima to help him during his battle with the demon Hidimba.

Mridani is also identified with the goddess Parvati, consort of the god Shiva. In Hindu iconography, she is depicted as the goddess of fertility, holding a trident, and is often shown seated on a lotus flower. The name Mridani is believed to mean 'pleasing to the mind' or 'beloved'.
